analogy.name: A four-act short film
analogy.line: A STAR story is like a short film in four scenes: establish the setting (situation), introduce your role (task), show the main scene (action), and end on the outcome (result).

behavioral.caption: A STAR story has four beats: set the scene, say what you owned, walk through what you did, and end on what changed.
steps: Scene one sets the location in a line or two. Interviewers do not need the backstory or names. Too much setting eats time you need for the action.
Scene two says your role. State what was yours to do, because the panel is scoring you, not the team. Say I, not we, where it is true.
Scene three is the main event and the longest beat. Walk through what you did in order, with the reasoning behind each choice. This is where you show your skill.
The ending is what changed, with a number if you have one. Then stop talking. A clear finish is stronger than rambling on or hedging the outcome.
